DeviceCodeFlowCallback.summary: Optional device-code-flow callback invoked for SqlAuthenticationMethod.ActiveDirectoryDeviceCodeFlow. When , the provider's default callback (which writes the device-code instructions to the console) is used.

ApplicationClientId.summary: Optional Entra ID application (client) id. When , the SqlClient first-party application id is used and WAM broker mode is forced on (regardless of ) when running on Windows.

UseWamBroker.summary: Windows-only setting to control whether the provider uses the WAM broker for interactive authentication. Defaults to when you provide a custom . Otherwise, WAM broker mode is used automatically on Windows.

AuthenticationLoggingCallback.summary: Gets or sets an optional callback for authentication diagnostics.
AuthenticationLoggingCallback.remarks: Defaults to . Receives immutable values independently of SqlClient EventSource collection. Includes direct MSAL messages, a reviewed non-PII subset of Azure Identity diagnostics, and SqlClient authentication lifecycle diagnostics. It does not receive every existing trace emitted by the provider or diagnostics from application-created credentials. A configured callback receives every eligible severity, including Verbose. Consumers control filtering using . A null callback disables callback delivery without restricting EventSource collection. It may be invoked concurrently on authentication threads and must execute synchronously, be thread-safe, return promptly, and not throw exceptions. Do not use async lambdas (async void): exceptions after an await cannot be isolated by the provider. For asynchronous sinks, synchronously enqueue into an application-owned bounded buffer and observe processing failures in the consumer. Do not start authentication synchronously from the callback. As a defensive safeguard, the provider catches nonfatal synchronous callback exceptions, reports a sanitized EventSource diagnostic, and allows authentication to continue. Logging triggered by the callback is not forwarded recursively. Options are copied when the provider is constructed; subsequent changes have no effect.

EnableMsalPiiLogging.summary: Gets or sets whether direct MSAL flows may send PII-bearing messages to the callback. Defaults to false.
EnableMsalPiiLogging.remarks: Requires a non-null . PII-marked authentication messages are never forwarded to SqlClient EventSource. This setting has no effect on Azure credential diagnostics: unsafe support logging, account-identifier logging, and HTTP content logging remain disabled. It does not enable PII logging for other provider operations. Obtain appropriate consent and protect sensitive logs when opting in.
